name: Blight

facts.text: A Blight Controller in the Cursed Forest brings out eight Fire Blights, then four Late Blights, then two Flesh Blights, and only then Blight itself.
Blight is level 70, 30,000 health: 'Bloody bones fly from all directions... forming a single giant skeleton', then 'Blight has taken it's true form! It turns its deadful stare upon you!'
The four-stage blight as a sickness of the wood's earth is Living Server lore.

In Cath Maige Tuired, Dian Cécht, his sons Octriuil and Miach and his daughter Airmed sing over the well Sláine, and the mortally wounded cast into it come out whole; the Fomorians fill it with stones carried from the river Drowes at Ochtriallach's bidding.
facts.source: Cath Maige Tuired (The Second Battle of Mag Tuired)

facts.text: In the same tale Dian Cécht kills his son Miach; 365 herbs grow from Miach's grave, one for each joint and sinew; Airmed lays them out on her cloak and her father mixes them so that their right use is lost.
facts.source: Cath Maige Tuired (The Second Battle of Mag Tuired)

facts.text: Living Server lore: the druids of Lough Gur reading the blight as the well of Sláine run backward, the soil giving back what was put into it.

story:
A crop disease does not arrive all at once. It comes in stages, and the farmers of Hibernia know the names: the fire blight that scorches the leaves, the late blight that rots the root, and the blight in the flesh that the old women do not name at all. The earth of the Cursed Forest learned all three when the court bargain broke there, and something in that earth learned to be them. The sickness has a will.

It comes up out of the ground in the same order, as if something in the soil sent them: eight fire blights first, smouldering things; then four late blights; then two of flesh, and that is when the wise go home. And if a band is foolish enough to kill all of those, the blight gathers the bones of everything it has ever killed out of the soil in a whirling cloud of gore and stands up as a single giant skeleton, and turns its dreadful stare on whoever is left. The Sylvan call that its true form. Nobody has asked them how they know. The farmers of Ardee burn their fields when they see the first sign of fire blight, and pray it never reaches the third.

The druids of Lough Gur keep an older account of sickness than the farmers' list, and they give it whenever the blight comes up in talk. When the Tuatha Dé Danann fought the Fomorians at the second Mag Tuired, their physician Dian Cécht had a well called Sláine, and he and his son Octriuil and his daughter Airmed sang spells over it. The Tuatha's dead and dying were thrown into it as they fell, and they came out of it whole and went back to the battle the next day. When the Fomorians learned of the well, Ochtriallach son of Indech had every man of them carry a stone from the river Drowes and throw it in, until the well was a cairn.

There had been a quarrel in Dian Cécht's house before that. His son Miach was the better physician, and the father killed him for it, and out of Miach's grave grew three hundred and sixty-five herbs, one for each joint and sinew of the body. Airmed spread her cloak and laid them out on it in order, each by the part it healed. Her father came and mixed them all together, so that no one should know their right use.

The druids think the blight of the Cursed Forest is something like Sláine run backward. The court wood's earth was a garden, kept and sung over, and when the bargain broke the singing stopped and the soil kept only the habit of giving back what was put into it. Into the well went the wounded, and out came the whole. Into the wood's earth went everything the wood had killed, and out of it comes the blight, stage by stage, fire and rot and flesh, and last of all the bones, gathered into a body that does not know it is dead. Derbáil of Ardee's grandmother had never heard of Sláine, and put it in fewer words: the ground gives back what it is given. The warriors who break the skeleton find the earth clean for a season. Then the first fire blight shows on the leaves again, and the Ardee farmers reach for their torches.
legend: It is a gauntlet, not a fight: eight fire blights, four late blights, two flesh blights, then Blight itself. Pace the healers and the mana across all four waves. Its true form has a dreadful stare; stay spread and do not draw other things in the forest meanwhile. Pace the healers and mana across all four stages; the skeleton is the hardest and comes last. Superstition: burn a pinch of salt before you start, as the Ardee farmers do before harvest. Nicknames: 'the four', 'the rot'. Ardee farmers burn a pinch of salt before the realm's bands go in, and the bands have taken up the habit.

aggro: The earth splits and something smoulders out.

loremasterTopic.text: The sickness of the Cursed Forest's earth. It comes as fire, rot and flesh, and then as a skeleton of every bone it ever took.

bookPage: From Derbáil of Ardee's list: grandmother said there are three blights and every farmer knows two. The fire blight that scorches, the late blight that rots, and the third, which she would not name but called the blight in the flesh. The Cursed Forest has all three in its earth, she said, and a fourth thing that comes after them, built out of the bones of everything the first three killed. I asked how she knew. She said her own grandmother saw it stand up once, from the edge of the wood, and went home and burned every field she had.
